verification.note: Traced by reading, not run. upload.py:134-135 allows the overwrite and uploads.py:82-87 emits scan.complete. webhook.py:105 and indexer.py:1125 run reconcile, which calls _reset_loft_refs_with_new_vtt (indexer.py:488). That function resets a loft only when _loft_needs_reset is true, and indexer.py:138-139 returns False once the loft is chunked. No mtime or hash comparison exists in addons/intelligence/app. _index_loft_vtt reads the VTT only when the task runs (whisper.py:1731-1763). test_spec_addon_001_loft_with_chunks_is_not_requeued (test_loft_vtt_sidecar.py:396) pins the no-requeue as deliberate for an unchanged VTT, and no test covers a changed one. Limits: scan.complete shows the user nothing beyond a list refresh, so 'look handled' is an inference. A per-file reindex route exists (intelligence routers/files.py:210), so this is correctable by hand if the route is reached; whether the UI offers it was not traced.

upload.py:134-136 skips the 409 for a subtitle over an existing file, and non-subtitle files still get 409. useUpload.ts:97-103 and :136-138 have no prompt. os.replace (atomic_write.py:61) discards the old bytes and _finish_subtitle_upload records nothing about them. The overwrite is deliberate and documented: docs/reference/api.md:184, docs/user-guide/upload-and-fileops.md:16, known-issues.md:266-267 and test_a_second_upload_replaces_the_file. Those documents state the replacement but not that the old text cannot be recovered.

The mechanics hold only on a normalization-sensitive filesystem, and the project declares a different host. docs/specs/nfc-tolerant-name-matching.md:18-21 states production is macOS APFS bind-mounted into containers and that opening a path works in either form because the host ignores normalization; :386-388 says direct exists(), open() and rename() calls on a built path are not affected. So upload.py:129 and :134 target_full.is_file() finds a decomposed sidecar there, and os.replace at atomic_write.py:61 replaces it, leaving one file. The only sensitive environment found is ubuntu CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:26), which is not normal use under the threat model. On such a filesystem the trace through subtitle.py:83-102 and :129-136 is accurate. The same exact-path test applied before this change, by the r4 record of upload.py:132-133, so the doubling would not be new either. This rests on the spec's statement; an NFD replacement was not run on the real mount.

Mutation reasoned, not run. test_an_existing_file_of_another_type_still_refuses_the_upload uses note.md, which fails the is_subtitle_file half at upload.py:134. No backend test uploads over a directory with a subtitle name: test_upload.py creates only the folders at :77 and :178, and backend/tests/test_sidecar_match.py:104 makes a Clip.vtt directory for matching, not for an upload. With is_file() removed, init answers 200, os.replace at atomic_write.py:61 raises on the directory, upload.py:235 does not catch it, and the cleanup at :246-247 is skipped. decisions.md:71 walked the guard by hand.

Same defect and same trace as the claude-read finding: upload.py:134-135, uploads.py:82-87, indexer.py:138-139, :488 and :620, whisper.py:1731-1763, decisions.md:67. Traced by reading, not run. files.py:1358 calls read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig") with no guard, main.py has no exception_handler, and files.py:1354-1356 answers 413 over 5 MB. upload.py:226-234 checks declared size only, and :249-250 finishes with no content check, so the upload answers 200 after the good file is gone. The failure is also silent in the player: useShellCaptions.ts:67-69 turns a non-OK response into empty cues, and :78 reports the state as unavailable with no error. A non-empty sidecar list also keeps the auto-generated track out (useShellCaptions.ts:43-51). test_subtitle.py has no match for shift, cp932, sjis, utf-8-sig or UnicodeDecodeError. A Shift-JIS .srt is ordinary input for this Japanese-language use, so it fits the threat model. The read failure predates the change; the loss of a working track comes from cde9bc7a3.

Same reason as the claude-read finding. The claim is conditional on a normalization-sensitive filesystem, and docs/specs/nfc-tolerant-name-matching.md:18-21 and :386-388 declare the production host resolves direct path operations through normalization, so upload.py:134 is_file() finds the NFD sidecar and atomic_write.py:61 replaces it. The cited test_listing_call_inventory.py:3-6 describes a different hazard: a listing compared with a stored name, not an exact-path open. decisions.md:17 walked NFD on that mount and shows a listing-compare path working there. On a sensitive filesystem the trace through subtitle.py:83-98 and :119-136 is accurate, and it was not run on the real mount.

specification_compliance: docs/reference/api.md:184 and docs/user-guide/upload-and-fileops.md:16 match upload.py:134-136: a subtitle replaces, and anything else at the path answers 409.
known-issues.md:265-268 matches the code on replacement and on the subtitle-only folder staying unlisted until a scan.
known-issues.md does not record that a replaced .vtt leaves a chunked loft's transcript stale, or that an unreadable replacement discards a working track.
potential_unspecified_behavior: No document says whether replacing a .vtt should re-index a loft that already has transcript chunks.
No document says whether a subtitle upload should validate encoding or the 5 MB serving limit before it replaces a working file.
A detail page already open in a second tab keeps its old track list after a subtitle upload until it is reloaded (decisions.md:69).
regression_risks: A replacement that cannot be decoded removes a working track, and the upload still reports success (upload.py:249-250, files.py:1358).
Ask and search can answer from captions the user has already replaced (indexer.py:138-139).
Each subtitle upload now runs a full Intelligence reconcile through scan.complete, as other uploads already do; a folder of subtitles triggers one per file.
test_coverage: Pinned by test_sidecar_subtitles_follow_video.py: replacement, a failed or cancelled second upload keeping the first, the scan.complete payload, and 409 for another file type.
Not pinned: the is_file() half of upload.py:134; a replaced VTT against chunked transcripts; a non-UTF-8 or over-5 MB replacement; a subtitle-only folder before a scan.
Replacement tests use ASCII names only. test_a_decomposed_sidecar_name_lands_under_the_composed_target covers rename only.
